decision: The map is the screen and the details live in a bottom sheet with three snap points, the pattern popularized by ride-hailing apps
why: 'Where is it?' is the only question in the first second; the sheet answers the second question (who, what, when) without leaving the map.
alternative: A timeline list with a small map thumbnail.
value: The answer is visible at a glance; details are one drag away.

decision: The courier position and ETA are computed from the dispatch time and the shared world clock, not animated on a timer
why: Tracking must agree with Counter and Mesh; scrubbing the world clock or reloading shows the same position everywhere.
alternative: A CSS animation that loops along the route.
value: One source of truth for time across the consumer app and the ops tools.

decision: The sheet handle is a real button: click cycles peek → half → full, arrow keys resize it, and dragging snaps to the nearest point
why: Drag-only sheets exclude keyboard and switch users; transforms keep the drag at 60 fps.
value: The same sheet works with touch, mouse, keyboard and reduced motion.

decision: Courier positions arrive as carrier webhooks through the partner gateway and fan out to the app over a push channel
why: Polling the carrier from every phone would multiply partner calls; the adapter normalizes each carrier once.
alternative: Each app polls the carrier API.
value: Partner calls stay constant as users grow (target [value] per order).

decision: Messaging the courier offers three quick replies instead of a keyboard
why: Couriers are riding; short, predictable messages are safer to read than free text.
value: Faster handoffs with less distraction for the courier.
